title: objectstack verify reports "✓ verify passed" (exit 0) on a stack that os validate, os build and os lint refuse — and the published CLI docs do not document verify
body:
QA-source: #21318 · cli.verify-verdict-exit-mapping · path step ③

## Summary

`docs/NORTH-STAR.md` defines done as: an app "过了验证才算做好 — … `objectstack verify` 在它上面是绿的". On 17.6.0, `objectstack verify` is green on a stack that every authoring gate refuses, so an author (human or AI) who uses the documented done-bar gets a false green.

## Reproduction (published `@objectstack/cli@17.6.0`, blank scaffold + a small task app)

Plant three mistakes the author-time registry catches:
- `Field.lookup('tasks_app_projects', …)` (no such object);
- an action `visible: 'done != true'` (bare reference instead of `record.done`);
- a list column `{ field: 'priority' }` that is not a field.

Then:

| command | exit | output |
|---|---|---|
| `npx os validate` | 1 | `✗ Author-time rules failed (3 issues)` — `expression-invalid`, `object-reference-unknown`, `list-view-field-unknown`, each located with a prescription |
| `npx os build` | 1 | same three |
| `npx os lint` | 1 | same three as errors |
| `npx objectstack verify` | **0** | `✓ tasks_app_note (2 fields) ✓ tasks_app_project (2 fields) ✓ tasks_app_task (5 fields) ── 3 verified, 0 gaps, 0 FAILED …` then `✓ verify passed — no runtime failures` |

`verify --help` describes it as CRUD round-trip fidelity plus the RLS invariant, so it does not consult the authoring gates at all — and the run gives no hint that the stack it just passed is one the build refuses to ship.

Separately, the published CLI reference (`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`) has no `os verify` section; `grep -rn "os verify\|objectstack verify" content/docs` (excluding generated references and release notes) returns nothing. A newcomer cannot learn from the docs what verify proves and what it does not.

## Expected

Either verify refuses (or at least reports, non-zero) a stack the author-time gates reject — so "verify is green" implies "validate is green" — or its pass line states what it did not check and the docs say to run `os validate` first. And `os verify` gets a section in the published CLI reference.
